name: Mini
assembly: Cape Town, South Africa (BMC/Leyland South Africa)

length.sourceNote: Saloon figure. The infobox gives 3,299 mm for the estate and commercial variants, recorded on the estate trim below.

width.sourceNote: The infobox gives two figures, 1,410 mm and 1,530 mm, with the wider one qualified as "up to, with widest 'sportspack' factory wheel-arches" — not the standard car, so the narrower figure is recorded here.

wheelbase.sourceNote: Saloon figure. The infobox gives 2,138 mm for the estate and commercial variants, recorded on the estate trim below — corroborated independently by a Dutch-registered 1966 Morris Mini estate at 2,140 mm (RDW).

kerbWeight.sourceNote: The infobox gives a single unattributed range, 580-686 kg, for the whole 1959-2000 model line and every trim — not a measurement of one car. Recorded here as the lower bound per project convention; per-trim figures sourced from Dutch registration records are recorded on individual trims below.

engine.configuration: water-cooled inline-4, single carburettor, BMC A-Series

displacement.sourceNote: The engine fitted at the August 1959 launch, transversely mounted with the gearbox in the sump. This displacement remained the base engine until the 1980 Mini City replaced the 850 model.

power.sourceNote: 34 bhp (SAE gross), converted at 1 bhp = 0.745699872 kW. The 1959 introductory figure; no separate output is given in the article for the base engine at later dates.

mass.sourceNote: Dutch registration record for a 1974 Morris Mini 850 — an individual car, not a manufacturer specification, but the only per-trim figure available since Wikipedia gives only the model-wide 580-686 kg range.

dragCoefficient.sourceNote: The Wikipedia drag-coefficients list gives 0.48 for the 'Rover Mini', dated 1998 — recorded on the 1990s Cooper trim below rather than here, since applying a figure explicitly dated to the car's last decade onto its 1959 launch spec would overstate how well this is sourced.

frontalArea.sourceNote: Derived, not published: the site's standing 0.85 x width x height approximation, using the generation's saloon width and height (1,410 x 1,346 mm).

engine.configuration: water-cooled inline-4, twin SU carburettors, BMC A-Series

displacement.sourceNote: Introduced in 1961 at 997 cc; replaced in 1964 by a longer-stroke 998 cc unit that remained until the Mark II Cooper was dropped in 1969. The longer-lived of the two displacements is recorded here — RDW's registration record for a 1968 car (below) confirms the 998 cc engine was current by then.

power.sourceNote: 55 bhp (SAE gross) for the original 997 cc engine at its 1961 introduction, up from the standard car's 34 bhp; converted at 1 bhp = 0.745699872 kW. No output figure is given in the article for the later 998 cc engine specifically.

mass.sourceNote: Dutch registration record for a 1968 Morris Mini Cooper Mark II, badge and 998 cc displacement matching this trim — an individual car, not a manufacturer specification.

engine.configuration: water-cooled inline-4, twin SU carburettors, nitrided-steel crankshaft, BMC A-Series

displacement.sourceNote: Introduced April 1964, the largest of three Cooper S displacements (970, 1,071 and 1,275 cc) and the only one to stay in production, until the UK Cooper S was discontinued in 1971.

power.sourceNote: 76 bhp (SAE gross), converted at 1 bhp = 0.745699872 kW. This car won the Monte Carlo Rally outright in 1964, 1965 and 1967 — it also finished first, second and third in 1966 before being disqualified over a headlamp-circuit technicality.

mass.sourceNote: RDW's individual-car registration records for two 1963 Morris Mini Cooper S cars (1,071 cc, not this trim's 1,275 cc) disagree by 22% — 535 kg and 690 kg for the same badge and year — too wide a spread to trust as a figure for this trim, and no Dutch record exists for the 1,275 cc S specifically. Wikipedia gives only the model-wide 580-686 kg range.

engine.configuration: water-cooled inline-4, single carburettor, BMC A-Series

displacement.sourceNote: The Austin Seven Countryman and Morris Mini-Minor Traveller launched in 1960 with the same 848 cc engine as the saloon. Later cars badged '1000' carried the larger 998 cc engine — the RDW-sourced mass below is for a 1969 '1000 Estate' and likely reflects that heavier, later powertrain rather than the 1960 launch spec.

wheelbase.sourceNote: Infobox figure for 'estate and commercials', corroborated independently by a Dutch-registered 1966 Morris Mini 3-door at 2,140 mm (RDW).

mass.sourceNote: Dutch registration record for a 1969 Morris Mini 1000 Estate — an individual car, not a manufacturer specification, and the '1000' badge implies the larger 998 cc engine rather than this trim's 1960 launch-spec 848 cc unit.

engine.configuration: water-cooled inline-4, fuel-injected (single-point from 1991, multi-point from 1997), catalytic converter, BMC A-Series

displacement.sourceNote: The Cooper name was relaunched by Rover in 1990-91 and went into full production in late 1991, using the same 1,275 cc engine as the 1960s Cooper S, now fuel-injected and catalysed to meet emissions rules — a multi-point injection system replaced the earlier single-point system in 1997.

dragCoefficient.sourceNote: Listed for the 'Rover Mini', dated 1998, which places it against this trim rather than the visually near-identical 1959 launch car. The body shape barely changed across the whole run, so the figure likely holds for earlier trims too, but the source dates it to 1998 specifically.

hero.alt: Cream-coloured 1959 Morris Mini-Minor photographed from the front three-quarter angle, showing the round headlamps, full-width front grille and registration plate 621 AOK
hero.caption: 621 AOK — the first Mini built, on display today at the Heritage Motor Centre. Round headlamps, sliding windows and external door hinges all mark it as a pre-1969 Mark I.

gallery.alt: Red 1964 Mini Cooper S rally car with Monte Carlo Rally number 52 on the bonnet, four spotlights above the grille and the registration AJB 44B
gallery.caption: A 1964 Cooper S in rally trim — the car that won the Monte Carlo Rally outright three times in the 1960s.

gallery.alt: Cutaway display Mini with transparent body panels, showing the transversely mounted engine over the front wheels, the four-seat cabin and the exposed chassis
gallery.caption: The whole idea in one photograph: engine and gearbox packed sideways over the driven wheels, leaving the rest of the floorpan for people.

gallery.alt: Yellow Mini Clubman photographed from the front three-quarter angle, showing the squared-off nose and rectangular grille that distinguish it from the round-nosed original
gallery.caption: The 1969 Clubman's squared-off nose, styled by Roy Haynes, ran alongside the unchanged round-front original for the rest of the car's life rather than replacing it.
